text: Reproduce heap pollution: put an `Integer` into a `List<String>`. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: ___;                                // a raw type: a warning, not an error
catch (ClassCastException e) { System.out.println("failed at the READ: " + e.getMessage()); }
explanation: Verified: it prints `[42]`, then fails at the read with a class cast the source never contains. At run time the list holds `Object` references and is happy to take an `Integer`; the failure arrives later, in a compiler-inserted cast. That distance between cause and symptom is why unchecked warnings mark exactly where the compile-time guarantee has a hole.
